opportunities.funder: Carnegie Trust for the Universities of Scotland
opportunities.title: Undergraduate Tuition Fee Grants

amount.raw: Our grants cover the cost of tuition fees, up to £1,820 per year for a full-time degree course.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Individuals from low-income households who are ordinarily resident in Scotland (and have completed at least two years of secondary schooling or college education in Scotland, or can demonstrate a substantial and recent connection to Scotland) and who are ineligible for government tuition fee support. Must be enrolled on or hold an unconditional offer for an undergraduate degree course at an eligible Scottish HEI. Income thresholds based on household type.
opportunities.summary: Funds tuition fees for undergraduate students at Scottish higher education institutions who are not eligible for government tuition fee funding, primarily individuals from low-income households who withdrew from earlier study or are seeking asylum. Covers tuition fees up to £1,820 per year.

opportunities.funder: Carnegie Trust for the Universities of Scotland
opportunities.title: Carnegie-Morgan Scholarship

amount.raw: Full tuition fees for the MSc in Biodiversity and Taxonomy of Plants plus an additional living-cost bursary of £1,200.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scottish-domiciled students from low-income households (per income thresholds) who are ordinarily resident in Scotland, have been accepted onto the MSc Biodiversity and Taxonomy of Plants (full-time or part-time) at the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh/University of Edinburgh, are entitled to remain indefinitely in the UK, have drawn down SAAS living-cost loan support, are not eligible for public grant funding for the course, and do not already hold a postgraduate degree.
opportunities.summary: A partnership scholarship between Carnegie Education Fund and the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh supporting Scottish-domiciled students from low-income households to undertake the MSc in Biodiversity and Taxonomy of Plants (SCQF Level 11) in plant science and botany, covering full tuition fees and providing a £1,200 living-cost bursary.
